sources.facts: Text pp45-47: Matron cottage is single-storey masonry with two hipped corrugated-steel roofs and west/east verandas; mixed brick/render/limewash on sandstone base. West skillion zincalume veranda has a north-end timber bathroom. South boundary has a stabilized arched doorway, protected by clear acrylic. North parlour has a bay window. Later east rooms/vestibule, veranda timber posts and boarded balustrade; chimneys. Most historic cell ranges are gone. No copyrighted plans/photos viewed.
Current three adjoining Yards1,3,4, Matron Cottage in Yard4 and substantial enclosure wall remains. No reconstruction of lost roofed prison ranges.
Actual construction contractor scope: gabion walls, loading-dock concreting, driveway/disabled access, decorative-rock courtyards and pedestal paving. Text only; copyrighted photographs unused.

Operator2021-22 annual report: centre opened25March2022, new multipurpose/retail/office spaces and interpretation landscape, redundant structures removed, perimeter walls conserved and cottage veranda timber details reconstructed. All operator images unused.

On-site2021 construction update: old visitor centre removed; displayed Separate Apartment footings covered for protection. New centre follows their alignment; new opening made in Degraves Street gabion wall and precast footings installed.

Institute of Architects event: Liminal/Snøhetta concept, actual detailed design/exterior finishes/documentation/site administration by MCA Architects. This does not establish that every competition-render element was built. No photographic pixels adopted.

Builder’s attributed construction statement: modern centre perches above ground on concrete joists to protect archaeology, with rock-filled gabion baskets substituting sandstone. Exterior roof/window sections remain unsurveyed.
